response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile full-stack engineer with strong testing, teaching, and open-source credentials, but does not meet the core hard requirement of 8 years of C++ programming — the only substantive C/C++ exposure is roughly 7 months at National Instruments plus an academic thesis project. The career trajectory is overwhelmingly web/product-oriented (TypeScript, Node.js, Ember, D), with limited evidence of building or leading large-scale cloud compute platforms, and no formal technical-leadership role owning platform strategy. The high-throughput microservices work at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby is the closest match but was in D, not C++, and was an individual-contributor role.
strengths: Low-latency, high-throughput microservices experience (millions of req/s at Sociomantic)
Strong mentoring/knowledge-sharing record: workshops, courses, conference talks, open-source tooling
Broad polyglot engineering breadth plus DevOps/CI/CD, Docker, and Kubernetes exposure
concerns: C++ experience far below the 8-year minimum (under one year, from 2014-2015)
No demonstrated ownership of large-scale cloud compute platform architecture
No formal technical-leadership role mentoring cloud/DevOps engineers or setting platform strategy

key_factors.factor: Large-scale infrastructure / cloud compute platform experience
